newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Sept 23, here are some of the top stories reported in U.S. technology trade publications.

INFOWORLD - Software developer Sundial Systems Corp. has discovered a problem with the new version of International Business Machines Corp's OS/2 Warp operating system that causes crashes in some applications, InfoWorld reported in its Sept. 23 issue.

While search engines are among the most popular sites on the Internet's World Wide Web, the race is on to develop products that will more accurately meet the needs of users searching for specific information in the vast computer network, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - Hardware and software companies are rushing to meet demand for more manageable personal computer systems, Information Week reported in its Sept. 23 issue. Cost of ownership of a Windows 3.x PC on a LAN has fallen to $11,000 a year from $13,000 and could fall another 50 percent by 2000, according to an analyst.
Lockheed Martin Corp will standardize its 120,000 electronic mail users on Microsoft Corp's Exchange server, marking the biggest installation yet of the messaging platform, Information Week reported.

MACWEEK - Talk that Apple Computer is considering buying Menlo Park-based startup Be Inc and adopting its BeOS has drawn attention from the fact that in any case, BeOS will provide a modern, high-performance alternative to Mac OS when it is available within six months, MacWeek reported in its Sept. 23 issue.

MacWeek said pricing has not been set, but is expected to fall in the $100 to $200 area, with Power Computing Corp and other Mac OS licensees believed to be in discussions with Be to bundle its BeOS with their machines, MacWeek reported.
